summary: IPFIX is a standard way for devices to export information about network traffic flows. This RFC defines SNMP managed objects for monitoring IPFIX Exporters and Collectors, including basic configuration information.

eli5.summary: Some machines count the traffic passing by and send reports. This memo defines a standard dashboard so you can check those counters and reporters are working.

questions: how to monitor ipfix exporters with snmp
what is the ipfix selector mib
what is an ipfix transport session
subtitle: The SNMP tables a router or collector exposes so operators can see how its IPFIX flow export is configured and performing.

tldr.problem: IPFIX devices export information about IP traffic flows, but operators had no standard way to inspect how an Exporter or Collector is set up: which sessions, templates and backup paths it uses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two SNMP MIB modules. The IPFIX MIB has tables for transport sessions, templates, exports, the metering process, observation points and selection processes, plus optional statistics. The IPFIX SELECTOR MIB lists the standard filtering and sampling functions.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 5815. It is read-only monitoring: it does not define the full configuration of the Metering Process.

facts.label: Main tables in the IPFIX MIB

today: RFC 6615 is a Standards Track document that obsoletes RFC 5815, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of the IPFIX MIB and IPFIX SELECTOR MIB modules.

sections.title: Two MIB Modules for IPFIX Devices
sections.content:
RFC 6615 defines two MIB modules for monitoring IP Flow Information eXport (IPFIX) devices, meaning both Exporters and Collectors. It relies on the IPFIX architecture (RFC 5470), the IPFIX protocol (RFC 5101) and the information model (RFC 5102).

Most objects in the IPFIX MIB module must be implemented, while some are implemented according to the functionality of the equipment. Because the architecture allows filtering and sampling to reduce data volume, a second module, the IPFIX SELECTOR MIB, holds the standardized selection methods and is controlled by IANA. The full configuration of the Metering Process is out of scope.

The modules are written in SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580) and are read through SNMP.
sections.eli5: Two lists of gauges: one for how the traffic reports are sent and received, and one naming the ways a device can pick which traffic to count.

sections.title: Sessions, Templates and Definitions
sections.content:
The Transport Session table is the basis of the module. It lists every transport session between an Exporter and a Collector, with the transport protocol, and for UDP and TCP the source and destination addresses and ports. For SCTP it holds the association index from the SCTP MIB (RFC 3873). It also records the device mode (exporting or collecting), the configured template refresh parameters used over unreliable transports such as UDP, the IPFIX version and the session status.

The Template table lists all Templates and Options Templates sent by an Exporter or received by a Collector. It is indexed by the transport session index and the Observation Domain ID, and stores the Set ID and the time the template was last sent or received.

The Template Definition table lists the Information Elements inside each template, in order. Each entry gives the element ID, the encoded length, the enterprise number for enterprise-specific elements, and flags showing whether the element is used for scoping or as a Flow Key.

The RFC walks through one example: an Exporter at 192.0.2.22 exports over TCP to a Collector at 192.0.2.37 and over UDP to one at 192.0.2.44, both to destination port 4739. The Collector would hold the same entry except for a different index and a device mode of collecting.
sections.eli5: Think of a logbook of phone lines between two offices, a list of the report forms used on each line, and a list of the boxes on each form.

sections.title: Export Groups, Failover and Load Balancing
sections.content:
On Exporters, the Export table supports failover, load balancing and duplicate export to several Collectors. Entries that share an ipfixExportIndex and a Metering Process cache ID form a Transport Session group, and each member has a type. Every session in this table MUST have the device mode exporting.

  • Without grouping, each export index holds one session, and it MUST be primary.
  • For failover, a group has one primary session and any number of secondary sessions; no other types are allowed in such a group.
  • For parallel export or load balancing, all sessions in the group MUST have the same type, either parallel or loadBalancing.

The algorithms for failover and load balancing are out of scope. The RFC also gives an eight-step recipe a manager can follow to find the backup Collector for a given Exporter and Collector pair: find the session by address, note its index, read the template table, find the matching primary entry in the export table, then look up the non-primary entries and their session details.
sections.eli5: If the main delivery route breaks, the device can switch to a spare one. This table says which route is the main one and which is the spare.

sections.title: Metering, Observation Points and Selection
sections.content:
The Metering Process table is indexed by cache ID. Each cache holds Flow Records, may be run by a separate instance of the Metering Process, and has an active timeout and an idle timeout that decide when flows expire. A reference to an observation point group says where the records are gathered; if none is specified it MUST be zero.

The Observation Point table groups observation points by group ID. Each entry names its Observation Domain ID and points to the ENTITY MIB (RFC 4133) or the Interfaces MIB (RFC 2863). At least one reference MUST exist, and if both are given they MUST point to the same physical interface. A direction can also be given, such as ingress or both.

The Selection Process table lists the filtering and sampling functions applied to the packets seen for a cache. They are applied in increasing order of the selector index. A function without parameters points to the root of its subtree; one with parameters points to an entry in its parameter table. If no filtering or sampling is used, an entry SHOULD point to the Select All function, ipfixFuncSelectAll.
sections.eli5: Where the device watches the traffic, how long it keeps a tally open before reporting it, and which packets it bothers to count, each get their own table.

sections.title: Statistics and Relationships to Other MIBs
sections.content:
Four optional statistical tables augment the session, template, metering process and selection process tables. The session statistics hold the rate in bytes per second, and the counts of bytes, packets, messages, records, templates and options templates received or sent, plus discarded messages. The template statistics count data records per template. The metering process statistics count exported data records and unused cache entries. The selection process statistics count packets observed and packets dropped by the selection method.

Each statistical table has a discontinuity object holding a timestamp, which tells the management system that the counters may no longer be continuous.

The IPFIX MIB imports from SNMPv2-SMI, SNMPv2-TC, SNMPv2-CONF, the Interfaces MIB, the ENTITY MIB and the INET-ADDRESS MIB (RFC 4001). Implementing the ENTITY MIB or Interfaces MIB is OPTIONAL, but implementers who want to specify the physical entity SHOULD implement them. If one is missing, its column in the Observation Point table is zero.
sections.eli5: Optional counters keep score of how much was sent, and a marker tells you when a counter was reset so you do not trust a number that jumped.

sections.title: The IPFIX SELECTOR MIB
sections.content:
The SELECTOR MIB gives a home to the standard filtering and sampling functions. They MUST be registered under ipfixSelectorFunctions, which is 1.3.6.1.2.1.194.1.1, in a sub-registry kept by IANA. The first entry is ipfixFuncSelectAll, which selects everything.

New functions require Expert Review. Experts check the requested objects for completeness and accuracy of the description, requests that duplicate existing functionality SHOULD be declined, and the smallest available OID SHOULD be assigned.

A function named Fx SHOULD form a subtree ipfixFuncFx with an availability object ipfixFuncFxAvail of type TruthValue, and a table ipfixFuncFxParameters if it takes parameters. Packet selection methods themselves are defined elsewhere (the PSAMP documents, RFC 5474 and RFC 5475) and are not part of this RFC.
sections.eli5: It is a menu of ways to pick which traffic to count. New menu items must be approved by a few experts so the menu stays tidy.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
No object in these modules has read-write or read-create access, so correct implementations cannot be altered through SNMP SET operations. Some readable objects may still be sensitive. The transport session and export tables may reveal network infrastructure, the metering process table may reveal information about the device, and the observation point table may reveal both. The selector functions contain no sensitive data now.

Implementations MUST provide the SNMPv3 security features, including authentication and privacy through the User-based Security Model (RFC 3414) with the AES cipher (RFC 3826). They MAY also support the Transport Security Model with a secure transport such as SSH or TLS/DTLS. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The gauges can only be read, not changed, but they could still tell a snoop how your network is built, so use the secure version of SNMP.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned ipfixMIB as { mib-2 193 } and ipfixSelectorMIB as { mib-2 194 }. The old IPFIX SELECTOR MIB registry defined in RFC 5815 was removed because this document discontinues its use.

IANA maintains a new sub-registry named IPFIX-SELECTOR-MIB Functions at the prefix 1.3.6.1.2.1.194.1.1, with Expert Review as the registration procedure. It starts with one entry: decimal 1, ipfixFuncSelectAll, described as select everything.
sections.eli5: IANA handed out two official numbers for the two lists and keeps a register of the counting methods.

items.label: secondary
items.desc: A backup session in a failover group.

items.desc: All sessions in the group export in parallel.

items.label: loadBalancing
